newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan banks to keep direct contact with HK, Macau.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan banks to keep direct contact with HK, Macau.

text.p: Taiwan's finance ministry said on Wednesday the island's banks would continue direct contacts with Hong Kong and Macau counterparts following Hong Kong's July 1 reversion to the rule of Taipei's arch rival, Beijing.

"Taiwan banks are allowed to continue direct contacts with Hong Kong and Macau banks after July 1 and, through Hong Kong and Macau banks, maintain indirect contact with mainland China's financial institutions," the ministry said in a statement.
The ministry added it would allow Taiwan banks to set up branches in Hong Kong and welcome Hong Kong banks to set up on the island.
"Maintaining Taiwan-Hong Kong financial communications after July 1 and further expanding those communications is the government's set policy," the ministry statement said.

It said it would soon announce rules allowing Taiwan banks to establish subsidiaries in Hong Kong and Macau under the same guidelines as those governing susbidiary set-ups by Taiwan banks in other countries.
Applications for establishing Hong Kong and Macau branches would be evaluated case by case, the ministry said.
The liberalisation followed the ministry's annoucement on Tuesday that it would allow domestic insurance companies to invest in all foreign securities, including Hong Kong's.
But such investment in China was still banned, the ministry said.
The ministry also said it has raised domestic insurers' foreign investment ceiling to 10 percent of total insurance funds from the previous five percent cap.
The ministry said local insurers had been allowed to invest in only 20 foreign stock markets, including the New York stock exchange. It did not specify the other 19 foreign markets.
